title: THE GAUNTLET · COMPROMISED RUNNING
vibe: green · hard on purpose · 45 minutes flat · you never stop moving, and every station hands you straight to the belt
why: Five hours of sleep, nothing sore, forty five minutes, and you want hard. Green. Yesterday your legs did sixty front squats a side and your shoulders did thirty presses a side, so today deliberately does not headline the squat or the overhead press. It headlines the two things that have gone quietest: the SWING and the HORIZONTAL PULL. The shape jumps as far from the last three days as the library allows. Monday was a ladder chain counted in rungs. Sunday was a descending chipper counted in a list. Friday was a running block bolted onto a density block. Today the run is not a block at all. It is the connective tissue: you run four hundred meters, you hit a station, you run four hundred meters, you hit the next one, and the clock never stops. The research came from the hybrid racing side of the house, a tradition this program has not touched since July seventh, and the idea it gave up is COMPROMISED RUNNING. Running clean is a cardiovascular workout. Running with flooded legs and disrupted breathing right off a station is a different skill entirely, and it is a skill you have never been asked for here, despite being the best runner in your own log by a wide margin. And you told me the single bell ladders came in under target on Monday. Noted. The volume today is written at the top of the range, not the middle.

blocks.title: WARM-UP · DAY A · SHOULDERS & SPINE & HAMSTRINGS
blocks.meta: ~6 min · Moves Method Day A · ONE PASS · unhurried, then one belt primer
blocks.format: mobility · one pass through the list, no rounds

items.name: SPINE AND SHOULDERS · one pass
items.detail: Shoulder dislocates with a towel or belt ×15 · thoracic rotations on all fours, 8 per side, eyes following the hand · overhead reach-out in a deep squat, 6 slow · wrist rocks 30 sec. Your shoulders did thirty presses a side yesterday and today asks them for rows and a devil's press, so open the front of them first.

items.name: HAMSTRINGS AND HIPS · one pass
items.detail: Jefferson curl, unloaded or 12 kg, 5 slow reps rolling down one vertebra at a time · single-leg goodmorning 8 per side · hamstring walkouts ×8 · active pigeon 30 sec per side. Everything today hinges. Load the hinge pattern with the hips already long.

items.name: BELT PRIMER · 3 min
items.detail: Walk 60 sec at 6 km/h, then jog 2 min at 11 km/h. Cadence high and light, around 170 steps a minute, shorter stride. You are about to run five separate legs on tired legs, so set the mechanics now while they are still fresh.

blocks.text: Day A off the Moves Method menu, last used 08-20 and the furthest back in the rotation. Day C ran yesterday, Day B ran Friday.

blocks.title: BLOCK 1 · THE GAUNTLET · 5 STATIONS, 5 RUN LEGS, ONE CLOCK
blocks.meta: ~25 min · 5 LAPS TARGET · STRETCH 6 LAPS · 2.0 km of running inside it · 20 kg KB · 16 kg KB · 2 × 22 kg DB
blocks.format: gauntlet circuit FOR TIME · one running clock · a 400 m run leg sits between every station · effort measured by laps finished, not by rounds of anything
blocks.workRest: There is no rest. The run leg IS the rest and it is not restful, that is the entire point. Start the clock at the first run leg and do not stop it until the carry finale is done. Transitions count as work.

items.name: THE LAP · read this once, then never look again
items.detail: ONE LAP = 400 m on the belt at 12.5 km/h, then straight to the station, then straight back to the belt. Five laps, five different stations, in this order. If the belt has no distance readout you trust, run 1:55 instead of 400 m. Do not pause the belt between laps, just step off and step back on.

items.name: LAP 1 · run 400 m → TWO-HAND SWING · 20 kg × 40
items.detail: The ski erg slot. Forty unbroken if you can, two sets of twenty if you cannot. Hips snap, arms are rope, bell floats to chest height and no higher. This is the biggest hinge volume in a week and it is the pattern that has gone quietest since Friday.

items.name: LAP 2 · run 400 m → BENT-OVER ROW · 2 × 22 kg DB × 20
items.detail: The sled pull slot. Hinge to about forty five degrees, back flat, both dumbbells to the hip pockets, elbows tight, a real pause at the top of every rep. Twenty reps with the pair. Horizontal pull is the other quality that has gone quiet, and it is the one you consistently rate highest.

items.name: LAP 3 · run 400 m → ★ WILDCARD · DEVIL'S PRESS · 2 × 16 kg × 14
items.detail: First devil's press anywhere in this log. Both bells on the floor, hands on the handles, drop to a push-up, feet back in, then in ONE movement swing both bells between your legs and throw them straight overhead to lockout. That is one rep. Fourteen of them. It is a burpee, a hinge and a press stitched together and it will spike your heart rate harder than anything else in the session. Then you go run. That is the joke and that is the training effect.

items.name: LAP 4 · run 400 m → RENEGADE ROW · 2 × 16 kg × 12 per side
items.detail: The rower slot, converted to pull plus midline. Plank on the bells, feet wide, row one bell to the hip WITHOUT letting the hips rotate a degree. Twelve per side, twenty four total. Your midline pays for this one, which is why the finisher later goes anti-rotation too.

items.name: LAP 5 · run 400 m → THRUSTER · 16 kg × 30
items.detail: The wall ball slot, and the only squatting in the session. Bell in the goblet rack, full squat, drive out of the hole and let the momentum press it overhead. Thirty reps. Light bell on purpose, because yesterday's legs and shoulders already paid, and this is a lung station, not a strength station.

items.name: FINALE · FARMER CARRY · 2 × 22 kg · 100 m UNBROKEN
items.detail: No run before this one, it comes straight off the thrusters. Pick both up, walk 100 m, and do not set them down. Not once. Grip work is a confirmed favorite and this is where the clock stops. Note your total time.

items.name: IF THE CLOCK ALLOWS · LAP 6
items.detail: If you finish the carry with more than four minutes left, run one more 400 m and repeat the swings at 20 kg × 40. You told me Monday's ladders came in easier than the target said they would, so the ceiling here is deliberately not capped. Tell me whether you took lap 6.

items.name: 📋 STILL OWED · a watch split
items.detail: This belt is still uncalibrated. Start the watch for the whole gauntlet and give me the total running distance and the average pace it shows. Five separate 400 m legs against a watch total is actually a better calibration than one clean run, because it averages out the starts and stops.

blocks.noteGreen: Seeded from Neupert #29-30 'The BIG 6' six-station single-bell circuit, restructured so the stations are separated by running instead of by rest. Volume is written at the top of the range on purpose. Take lap 6 if it is there.
blocks.text: The whole design rests on one idea from today's research: running clean and running off a station are different skills, and only one of them is in your log. Every lap here makes you find your stride again with your legs already flooded.

blocks.title: BLOCK 2 · THE HOLD · ANTI-ROTATION MIDLINE
blocks.meta: ~7 min · 2 ROUNDS · 2 × 16 kg KB · rest 30 sec between rounds
blocks.format: anti-rotation and anti-extension circuit · 2 ROUNDS, straight through
blocks.workRest: Straight through all three, rest 30 seconds, run it once more. TWO ROUNDS.

items.name: PLANK DRAG-THROUGH · 2 × 16 kg · 12 per side
items.detail: High plank with a bell outside each hand, feet wide. Reach under your chest with the opposite hand and drag the far bell across to the other side. Hips do not rotate and do not lift. Twelve per side, twenty four drags.

items.name: WEIGHTED DEAD BUG · 16 kg overhead · 14 total
items.detail: On your back, bell pressed straight up in one hand, low back pinned flat. Extend the OPPOSITE arm and leg long, then return. Seven per side. The overhead load is what turns a dead bug into real anti-extension work.

items.name: COPENHAGEN PLANK · 25 sec per side
items.detail: Top leg on a bench or chair, forearm down, lift the hips and hold. Adductors and lateral chain. Shorten it by using the knee instead of the foot if twenty five seconds is not there.

blocks.text: Yesterday's midline block was loaded LATERAL flexion, windmills and side planks. Today swings back to anti-rotation and anti-extension so the two halves of the midline alternate instead of stacking.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN · 3 MIN

items.name: WALK IT DOWN · 90 sec
items.detail: Belt at 5 km/h. Nose breathing only. Let the heart rate come off the gauntlet before you step away.

items.name: HAMSTRING AND CALF · 45 sec per side
items.detail: Standing hamstring reach, then a wall calf stretch. Two kilometers in five broken pieces plus forty swings is a lot of posterior chain.

items.name: DOORWAY PEC + LAT REACH · 30 sec per side
items.detail: Everything today pulled. Open the front back up.

blocks.text: Three minutes. The forty five went into the gauntlet, which is where you asked for it.

timer.emomUnit: gauntlet laps completed (400 m run + its station)
